resources.string: Reduce screen flicker at low brightness

DC Dimming adjusts the screen brightness by changing the circuit power supply rather than pulsing the screen backlight. This significantly reduces screen flicker in dark environments and minimizes eye strain, but may cause slight color distortion at very low brightness levels.
High Brightness Mode (HBM) boosts the display\'s peak luminance, making it easier to see in direct sunlight. Using this for extended periods can increase power consumption and generate more heat.
Power phone directly without charging battery
Resumes normal charging and Warp/VOOC immediately.
Phone runs purely off external power, 0 mA battery charging.
Bypass charging + clears thermal throttling mitigation so the CPU/GPU won\'t throttle during long gaming sessions.

Bypass charging routes power from the charger directly to the internal circuitry (VSYS), skipping the battery entirely. This prevents battery heat generation and protects battery health during intensive tasks like gaming.\n\nNote: Requires a charger to be connected.
Limit charging power to extend battery lifespan

Gentle charging caps the maximum Warp / SuperVOOC charging power and current to reduce chemical degradation and heat buildup in the battery cells.\n\nRecommended for overnight charging or whenever rapid top-ups are not required.
Touch responsiveness, sensitivity, and glove mode
Improve touch response and latency for gaming
Increase sensitivity for use with gloves

Hardware touch tuning directly controls the touchscreen digitizer controller:

• Game touch mode boosts the touch sampling response and applies gaming palm-rejection.
• Touch sensitivity adjusts the capacitive sensing threshold for lighter finger contact.
• Touch smoothing filters micro-jitter and stabilizes fast swipe trajectories.
• Glove mode maximizes capacitive sensitivity to detect touches through fabric and leather.
Adjust haptic feedback and vibration intensity

Hardware vibration tuning directly adjusts the boost converter voltage and drive gain of the internal linear resonant actuator (LRA). This controls the tactile punch and vibration strength across incoming calls, notifications, and interactive system haptics.
